questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, highlighters, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

options.A: marginal utility of X = price of X and marginal utility of Y = price of Y.
options.B: marginal utility of X plus marginal utility of Y is maximised.
options.C: marginal utility of X = marginal utility of Y. marginal utility of X price of X
options.D: = price of Y. marginal utility of Y

What will cause the supply curve of labour in a particular industry to shift to the left?

options.A: a fall in demand for the industry’s product
options.B: a greater use of machinery in the production of the industry’s output
options.C: a rise in wages paid in similar occupations in other industries
options.D: a weakening of trade union influence in the industry

What is not one of the roles prices play in a perfectly competitive market economy?

options.A: to provide a rationing mechanism for allocating goods between consumers
options.B: to provide incentives to producers to respond to changes in consumer demands
options.C: to provide information to consumers about the quality of different products
options.D: to provide information to producers about changes in consumer preferences

questions.questionText: Which commodities should a government tax if it wishes to make the tax system more progressive?

options.A: those for which demand is price elastic
options.B: those for which demand is price inelastic
options.C: those with an income elasticity of demand greater than one
options.D: those with an income elasticity of demand less than one

questions.questionText: The Chinese government is increasing the role of market forces in its economy. However, in 2008 it imposed temporary maximum price controls on energy and transport. Why might a government, committed to reducing central planning, introduce price controls?

options.A: to increase allocative efficiency
options.B: to increase the incentive for producers to raise supply
options.C: to reduce consumer demand
options.D: to reduce expectations of inflation

questions.questionText: What is typically associated with a relatively low level of income per capita in a country?

options.A: a high rate of saving
options.B: a low rate of economic growth in past periods
options.C: a low rate of inflation
options.D: a low rate of population growth

questions.questionText: What is likely to increase a country’s actual output in the short run but may reduce its long-run rate of growth of potential output?

options.A: an increase in the size of the government’s budget deficit
options.B: an increase in the size of the labour force
options.C: increased female participation in the labour force
options.D: increased government spending on education

questions.questionText: What is a likely consequence of an increase in cyclical unemployment?

options.A: a deficit on the current account of the balance of payments
options.B: a deterioration in the fiscal balance of the government
options.C: an increased rate of inflation
options.D: an increase in immigration

Why are high and variable rates of inflation likely to be harmful to long-run economic growth?

options.A: They hide relative price changes leading to a misallocation of resources.
options.B: They increase the real burden of household debt leading to lower consumption.
options.C: They lead to an increase in the household saving ratio.
options.D: They result in an increase in real interest rates.

questions.questionText: Economists have proposed that the best policy to promote development is ‘trade not aid’. What is implied by this proposal?

options.A: Developing countries should become self-sufficient and not rely on aid.
options.B: Developing countries should be given greater access to markets in developed countries.
options.C: Developing countries should use foreign aid to invest in their export industries.
options.D: Developing countries should use trade barriers to promote import substitution.

questions.questionText: What is likely to result from foreign direct investment in developing economies?

options.A: a reduction in local wage levels
options.B: a reduction in tax revenues in developing economies
options.C: a reduction in the range of consumer goods available to the local population
options.D: a worsening of net income flows from investments

questions.questionText: A regressive tax is defined as one where

options.A: all taxpayers pay the same absolute amount of their income in taxation.
options.B: high income earners pay a lower proportion of their income in taxes than low income earners.
options.C: high income earners pay less in taxes than low income earners.
options.D: high income earners pay more in taxes than low income earners.
